papers.title: Gravitational wave detection via photon-graviton scattering and quantum interference
papers.summary: We present a fully quantum field-theoretic framework for gravitational wave (GW) detection, describing the interaction as inelastic photon-graviton scattering. We demonstrate that for \textit{a coherent graviton state}, this microscopic model explicitly reproduces the standard classical geometric-optics time delay, providing a rigorous consistency test of the correspondence limit. We propose a detection scheme based on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, where the GW-induced spectral shifts render entangled photon pairs distinguishable. This encodes the gravitational signal into the modulation of photon coincidence rates --- a quantum observable robust against laser intensity noise. Furthermore, we show that non-classical graviton states, such as squeezed states, induce unique decoherence signatures, establishing theoretical bounds on gravitational decoherence and defining the operational limits for probing the quantum nature of gravity.

papers.title: Fast projections of two-dimensional light patterns using acousto-optical deflectors
papers.authors: Robbert Decruyenaere, Clara Tanghe, Senne Van Wellen, Karel Van Acoleyen
papers.summary: Precise and flexible control of structured light fields is essential for applications ranging from optical trapping and quantum simulation to microscopy and materials processing. Acousto-optical deflectors (AODs) are widely used in these settings due to their high speed, large damage threshold, and ability to generate steerable optical tweezers. Multi-tone driving offers a powerful alternative to slow sequential scanning, enabling the projection of complex patterns with high accuracy as rapid acoustic modulation averages out inter-spot interference. In two dimensions, however, intermodulation between tones in orthogonal AODs can reintroduce coherent artifacts. We present a fast, feedback-free AOD projection scheme based on an incommensurately staggered frequency lattice that intrinsically suppresses such artifacts. For separable two-dimensional target patterns, our method removes the need for scanning entirely, enabling substantially faster and highly accurate projections. We further extend the approach to non-separable images using a minimal scanning strategy that maintains rather high projection speeds. These results demonstrate that appropriately engineered multi-tone AOD driving offers an efficient and robust route to high-speed, high-fidelity generation of arbitrary intensity patterns.

papers.title: Probing fluctuations in photon emission statistics of spin injected quantum dots with time dependent electronic excitation
papers.authors: Chiran Wijesundara, Vincent Iglesias-Cardinale, Yuan Lu, Herbert Fotso, Bo Xu, Tim Thomay
papers.summary: Electrically spin-injected ensembles of InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots emit circularly polarized single photons, with the emission helicity determined by the spin polarization of the injected electrons. A ferromagnetic CoFeB spin-injection layer with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, combined with an MgO tunnel barrier, enables spin-polarized electron injection into the quantum-dot active region, resulting in circularly polarized photon emission at zero applied magnetic field. These devices realize direct spin-charge-photon conversion in an electrically driven, microelectronics-compatible quantum light source that operates without an external pump laser. Using an extended Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer with four detectors and time-tagged readout, we measure time-resolved photon-number statistics that resolve up to $|2\rangle$ Fock states within a single excitation cycle. While single-photon ($n=|1\rangle$) emission tracks the electrical excitation pulse as expected, the two-photon ($n=|2\rangle$) statistics exhibit pronounced fluctuations at multiple temporal positions within the pulse. These fluctuations vanish upon demagnetization of the spin-injection layer, establishing a direct link between the multi-photon emission dynamics and the spin polarization of the injected carriers. The observations indicate that spin injection controls not only the helicity of the emitted photons but also higher-order temporal correlations of the emission. The behavior is phenomenologically captured by inserting both a variable excitation mechanism and a set of multi-emitter collapse operators within a stochastic wave function evolution. The platform thus opens a route to electrically driven, spin-controlled single and multi-photon Fock-state sources and provides a testbed for spin-conditioned multi-emitter dynamics in solid-state quantum light sources.

papers.title: PhD thesis: Modes, States, and Symmetries in quantum Optics for quantum Information and Metrology
papers.summary: This thesis explores the role of modes, states, and symmetries in quantum optics, within the context of quantum information and quantum metrology. It proposes a unified framework to analyze how the modal structure of photonic fields, the statistical nature of states, and their symmetry properties determine the physical resources that can be exploited for quantum information processing and quantum parameter estimation. A first line of investigation develops a description of time-frequency degrees of freedom as continuous quantum variables, highlighting their richness for encoding and manipulating information. A second axis studies entanglement and collective variables, clarifying the link between physical resources and metrological gains, particularly in reaching ultimate precision limits. Interferometric scenarios of the Hong-Ou-Mandel type are then analyzed, and a general formalism centered on the notion of symmetry is developed. This framework enables the analysis of a broad range of situations and leads to several generalizations. Finally, the thesis examines the symmetries imposed by optical superselection rules and their consequences for the structure of quantum states and their operational performance, with the aim of providing a deeper understanding of the foundations of quantum optics.

papers.title: High-Fidelity Universal Quantum Gates in a Cryogenic Atom Array
papers.authors: Junlan Jin, Donghyuk Seo, Yue Shi, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, Waseem S. Bakr
papers.summary: Neutral atoms in optical tweezer arrays have emerged as a leading platform for quantum information processing. The fidelity of entangling gates mediated by Rydberg interactions has improved rapidly and is increasingly constrained by blackbody-radiation-induced transitions, which shorten Rydberg lifetimes and create contaminant states that can cause correlated errors. Cryogenic environments can suppress these transition rates by more than an order of magnitude. However, realizing a universal gate set in such an environment has remained an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate a universal quantum gate set in a cryogenic $^{133}$Cs atom array, with a single-qubit gate fidelity of 99.970(2)% and a raw two-qubit entangling-gate fidelity of 99.76(8)%, within the range of leading room-temperature implementations. The entangling gate uses direct single-photon coupling between the electronic ground state and a Rydberg $P$ state, avoiding scattering and light shifts associated with two-photon coupling. The gate operates at a modest Rabi frequency of $2π\times4.3$ MHz. The measured fidelity agrees with our error model dominated by atomic motion, indicating a straightforward route to higher fidelity through improved cooling, while the fundamental error contribution from Rydberg decay is below $3\times10^{-4}$. These results establish a path to entangling-gate fidelities substantially beyond the current state of the art through cryogenic suppression of Rydberg decay, reducing the overhead for fault-tolerant computation.

papers.title: Detuning-assisted cavity enhancement in spectroscopy
papers.authors: Subhasish Guha, Sourav Das, Francesco Albarelli, Aiman Khan, Elnaz Darsheshdar, Adam D. Wright, Animesh Datta
papers.summary: Cavity-enhanced spectroscopy is a widely used experimental technique. We show that detuning the cavity frequency from the transition of interest can enhance the precision for dipole moment estimation by up to two orders of magnitude beyond the improvement when the cavity is resonant with the transition. We show this for both classical continuous-wave (CW) and pulsed single-photon probes, even in the presence of losses. We trace this enhancement to a detuning-controlled redistribution of information between the light- and matter-like polaritons, with losses determining the optimal branch. We show that this enhancement remains accessible using conventional photodetection and time-correlated single-photon counting.

papers.title: Reversible photorefractive attack in continuous-variable quantum key distribution
papers.authors: Junxuan Liu, Yuchao Liu, Qingquan Peng, Piao Tan, Tao Wang, Peng Huang, Anqi Huang
papers.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers information-theoretic security, but device imperfections introduce implementation vulnerabilities. Experimental evidence of the security consequences of transmitter vulnerabilities in continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) remains limited. Here, we experimentally investigate a reversible photorefractive attack in a local-local-oscillator CV-QKD system. Moderate blue-light illumination reduces the modulation variance of a lithium-niobate IQ modulator to a stable value without appreciably increasing estimated excess noise. The variance recovers after illumination is removed. We elucidate the underlying physical mechanisms and develop an attack that exploits recovery to compromise modulation calibration. Receiver measurements confirm that the resulting calibration mismatch leads to overestimated channel transmittance and underestimated excess noise. Key rate calculations based on measured parameters yield a positive estimated rate when the correctly calibrated rate is nonpositive. Recovery can also make the preceding manipulation harder to identify through later inspection. This work provides the first system-level experimental evidence that a reversible photorefractive response can be exploited to compromise modulation calibration in CV-QKD. These findings highlight reversible changes in quantum transmitters as a practical security concern, motivating security analyses and protection strategies that account for both optical perturbations and subsequent recovery.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum Repeater Chains with Atom-based Quantum Processing Units and Quantum Memory Multiplexers
papers.authors: Shin Sun, Daniel Bhatti, Shaobo Gao, David Elkouss, Hiroki Takahashi
papers.summary: Quantum repeaters enable the generation of reliable entanglement across long distances despite the underlying channel noise. Nevertheless, realizing quantum repeaters poses a difficult engineering challenge due to various device constraints and design tradeoffs. Herein we propose and analyze an efficient hybrid quantum repeater design that integrates atom-based quantum processing units, spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources, and atomic frequency comb quantum memories. Our design leverages the strong spectrotemporal multiplexing capability of the quantum memory to enable high-rate elementary-link entanglement generation between repeater nodes. Transferring the photonic entanglement into matter-qubit entanglement, together with deterministic quantum operations, further enables reliable long-distance entanglement distribution. We analyze photon-loss channels in the hybrid architecture and propose suitable error-suppression strategies that are natively incorporated into our repeater protocol. Using numerical simulations, we demonstrate the advantages of our hybrid design for end-to-end secret key rates in a linear repeater-chain model. With continued advances in relevant hardware technologies, we envision that the proposed hybrid design is well suited for large-scale quantum networks.

papers.title: Single-Satellite Quantum Repeater Performance Analysis
papers.authors: Cameron Paterson, Jasminder S. Sidhu, Thomas Brougham, Sarah E. McCarthy, Daniel K. L. Oi
papers.summary: Satellite optical links may be able to extend quantum communication range beyond that which is possible through optical fibres which are constrained by exponential loss scaling. Quantum repeaters have been proposed to mitigate high channel losses in both fibre and satellite links. Although satellite quantum repeaters could improve entanglement distribution efficiency, the attempt rate is constrained by classical communication latency in the entanglement swapping step. Direct entanglement distribution does not suffer this latency and can therefore compensate for high dual-downlink losses by increasing the source rate. A systematic comparative analysis of repeater-assisted and direct entanglement distribution rates using a satellite is absent from the literature. In addition to entanglement distribution rates, a detailed analysis of the fidelity of entanglement distributed by repeater-assisted satellite links has yet to be performed. Here, we develop an in-depth framework for describing a space quantum link consisting of a single satellite and two ground stations. We compare the entanglement distribution rates of direct and repeater-assisted satellite entanglement distribution, taking into account variations in overpass geometry and quantum memory capacity. The long-term entanglement distribution performance to different pairs of major cities is also considered, and the altitudinal dependence is explored. Furthermore, we develop a Monte Carlo model of the repeater satellite to explore the effect that different memory management policies and capacities have on the waiting time statistics of memory qubits. From these statistics we calculate the fidelity distributions of the entangled pairs established between the ground stations. These results will inform mission design for future space-borne quantum repeater nodes, as well as requirements on space-based memory platforms.

papers.title: Multipartite Bell-Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger nonclassicality from interwoven frustrated down-conversion
papers.authors: Marek Żukowski, Paweł Cieśliński, Marcin Markiewicz, Konrad Schlichtholz
papers.summary: We present a theory of an interference process that starts with $N$ coherently pumped two-mode parametric down-conversion (PDC) sources, whose output modes are directed to $N$ observers such that each observer receives modes from two different source crystals. Each observation station is equipped with a locally controlled PDC crystal, coherently pumped with the source crystals, whose output modes are perfectly aligned with the input modes from the source PDCs. By varying the local phases of the input modes, perfect $2N$-photon interference can be observed in $2N$ single-photon registrations, one in each output mode of these $N$ local PDCs. The interference results from the indistinguishability of the origins of the detected $2N$ photons: either they all originate from the source PDCs or from the local PDCs. Bell-GHZ nonclassicality of the process emerges when one also considers situations in which at least one of the local PDC processes is blocked. In such cases, the $2N$-photon interference disappears. A ''lifted`` Clauser-Horne inequality is violated when its sole negative term, involving all observers with all local pumps active, is tuned to maximal destructive interference, while all other terms involve settings in which one of the local pumps is off.

papers.title: Optical Calibration of a Frequency-Domain-Multiplexed X-Ray TES Microcalorimeter Array via Photon-Number-Resolved Statistics
papers.authors: Giacomo Gorla, Bernard Sohl, Emanuele Taralli, Martin de Wit, Luciano Gottardi, Kevin Ravensberg, Kenichiro Nagayoshi, Davide Vaccaro, Hugo van Bohemen, Mio Poortvliet, Wolfgang Loeffler
papers.summary: Transition-edge sensor (TES) microcalorimeters for future X-ray space observatories require accurate low-energy calibration, a regime where conventional X-ray sources are limited by intrinsic linewidth, count rate, or experimental complexity. In this work, we investigate fibercoupled optical photons as a compact calibration tool for an Athena-like TES array. Optical pulses at 405 nm were generated with an acousto-optic modulator and delivered through an optical fiber onto a selected TES pixel inside a dilution refrigerator, via a dedicated cryogenic alignment interface. Externally triggered pulses were processed with an optimal-filter pipeline, including baseline subtraction, drift correction, and multi-Gaussian reconstruction of the pulse-height spectrum. The reconstructed spectra show resolved photon-number peaks consistent with the Poissonian statistics expected from an attenuated coherent source, reaching equivalent energies above 400 eV with a mean photon number exceeding 100 per pulse. The detector response was further tested for linearity by comparing the measured photon-number distributions against those predicted from the independently calibrated number of photons sent to the detector and a single, globally estimated detection efficiency, confirming Poissonian, linear behaviour across nearly two orders of magnitude in photon number. These results demonstrate that fiber-delivered optical photons can probe the few-eV to sub-keV response of Athena-like TES microcalorimeters, offering a practical and extensible framework for future low-energy calibration studies.
